As of the 15th of April, groups of people started to leave this place in Stubla and head in the direction of the border of Macedonia, because they thought that they would find salvation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And, sir, did you hear of any villagers who had attempted to return to their villages, and did they come back with stories about what they found there?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not so clear what you mean. Which villages are you talking about? Do you mean Delekare or Remnik village?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Let me now be specific, sir. Did any of the people, the 20.000, try to go home again; and if so, did they come back with stories about what they found? If you don't know, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: No. It's true that when some of them returned home, they found the houses looted and raided, some burned down, but this happened after some time, after the tenth day in Delekare and Remnik. The other part of the population fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And you fled with them, I understand, sir, on the 4th of May, and you decided to go to Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That is, on the 4th of May, driven out of poverty, misery and lack of foodstuffs and the constant danger threatening us, listening to the firearms, gunshots coming from the Serbian army and which were present in that area, seeing their movements, we felt completely insecure. This is why we decided, as a group of about 600 people, to leave that place and head towards the border with Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And you did that, I understand, sir, and you walked for a while and you stopped somewhere. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. On the 4th of May, at night, we moved from there. It was about 8.00 in the evening. We moved at night because we didn't want to be discovered by the Serbian forces and suffer as a result of that. So during our movements, we passed from Donja Stubla to Selishte village, then to Goden, then Jsufaj neighbourhood, and then we arrived in Seferaj village. It is situated --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That's fine. I understand you stayed there overnight and then the next morning you walked on to Rustaje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In Rustaje, we arrived sometime around 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And then something happened there, sir. Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Our group, which was heading towards Macedonia, when it arrived in Rustaje neighbourhood, we encountered Serb forces, military and paramilitary forces. We were surrounded by them. Then, under the threats and after they ransacked and searched us, we felt very tense and insecure. During this time, men were separated. Men beginning from 16 years of age up to 60 years of age were separated from the women and children. They took us away about 500 metres from the group and ordered us to kneel down and keep our hands above our heads. We were surrounded by the Serbian forces, among whom there were also paramilitaries who were always under the influence of drugs, and so their behaviour was very severe towards us. While we were there and being threatened with being killed, we suddenly heard the shouts and shrieks of our women and children who were present there. And when it became a very alarming situation, some of the military ordered us to get up, and at that moment the women and the children who were crying, shouting, they started to come towards us, to join us as a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. You were reunited with the women and children, and then I understand you went somewhere further. And how is it that you ended up going wherever it was you went? How did you know where to go, and how did you get there?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: During the time that we were reunited with our women and children, they ordered us to walk about one kilometre on foot, being escorted by them all the way. They were lined up on both sides of the group. And then they asked us to sit down when we found a meadow. And during the time that they ordered us to sit down in that meadow, the commander of that military unit came up to us with four paramilitaries and soldiers, with their weapons trained at us - at me, actually - and they threatened me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: They threatened me with words, asking me to give them explanation why we had called in NATO, and they began to insult me for being Albanian, and using other obscene words. They stayed with me for about one hour. I tried to keep calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: What language did they use to communicate with you?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: The language they used to communicate with me was exclusively Serbian, no other language.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right, sir. And after that hour, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Then we were ordered to move on in the direction of Presevo and a village, Hoxhe of Presevo. We were told not to turn our head, or if we dared move from the way, we would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Did you follow that instruction?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: At the beginning, we followed their instructions up to a point until when we thought that we started to deflect from the role because we were afraid that we would run up against some other forces. So someone among us who knew the terrain better said, "Let's go and take to the mountains," and this is what we did. The entire group took to the mountain and approached the border with Macedonia. That night, the entire group of deported citizens, we spent the night in Mal i Thate under the rain. And the next morning very early - it was about 3.00 in the morning - we set out, led by a person who knew the way but who had links with the Serbian forces. He told us where to go, but in exchange for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Okay. Finish your sentence and then I have a question. In exchange for that, what?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: This person who was certainly urged by the Serbian forces, asked us, the members of the group, to give him some amounts of Deutschmarks for him to show us the place. I think everything was done in collaboration with the Serbian forces, border forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: En route to this different border crossing, sir, did you meet up with other refugees from Zegra?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. In the Mal i Thate, there was another group who was stationed some days ago in -- in Presevo and other surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: They were about 300 other citizens. One of them knew the way, and he showed us the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right. And is it fair to say, sir, that together, the group you were with and the 300 other group, you joined into a combined group and crossed the border; is that right?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That is, our group and the other group joined together and crossed the border at that checkpoint, and we went over to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Sir, I just have a couple more questions. I'd like you to have a look at Exhibit 3, map 10 again, if you would. I said we'd come back to this map. Can you or would you, please, for the benefit of the Court, point the route that you took to the border. In other words, from Zegra, you went -- just trace on the pointer on the map, without commentary, just show the general area where you went and where you crossed the border on this map, if it's visible. Don't give us any detail, just show us the route you took. Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right. If you could do that, it would be very helpful. Start at Zegra, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: It is the Zheger village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... going to help. Thank you. Good.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: This is where the Zheger village is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: This is where the refugees were. Then we moved in this way, along this way that I'm showing you with my pointer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Then we passed Reka, the Jsufaj neighbourhood, Seferaj, Rustaje, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Into Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. We crossed over to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: All right. So if we look at the map, just so that the record reflects what you've done, if we look at Zegra and go -- there's also a compass point heading south. There are two arrows leading to the Macedonia border south of Zegra. You took the second arrow to the right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: The second arrow to the right, the one that I showed you. That was our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Just one more question, sir. When you returned to your village, can you tell us how you -- what state you found your village in? That is, Zegra.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: During the time that we were in Stubell, Lower Stubla, from the 5th of April, the Zheger village began to be torched. The houses were set on fire, the houses of the Albanian citizens, by the Serb military and paramilitary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, we'll get on better if you just listen to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Did you go back to your village of Zegra?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did, on the 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And when you got there, what condition did you find the Albanian houses to be in, in general?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: The houses of Albanians, in general, were burned down or -- either wholly burned down or partially burned down. Only a few of them remained intact. I may otherwise say that none of the houses managed to remain entirely intact. Most of them, about -- out of 120, they were totally burned, 420 partially burned, and only a small number more or less intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: How about the Serb houses?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI
utterances.text: The Serbian houses were all intact. When I was returning from Macedonia by car, whose owner drove me to my village, the local Serbs were getting ready to leave Zheger at those moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Would you -- those are all my questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examination tomorrow morning. Mr. Shabani, would you, during this adjournment, remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence. That includes members of the Prosecution team. Would you be back, please, at 9.00 tomorrow morning to conclude your evidence. We'll adjourn now until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.55 p.m.,
